questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A german-speaking country since I wished to improve my German language skills. Also a smaller student friendly city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was alright. The University was good at sending information about studentcard etc. (however a little bit confusing with insurance and documents needing to be send), and the hospital informed me well about dates and meeting points.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of offers from the university about introduction days to the city and uni, but it wasn't relevant for me since I was primarily at the hospital for an internship and already knew the city well from being there some time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. In Germany there's a big webside (WG-gesucht), where you can search for available rooms. I got a room at the first place I wrote and was lucky to get something super central, which I really appreciated.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There's a good network for finding rooms and a good flow in availabilities - I recommend living with people from the country you visit (in my case Germany).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Again,
WG-gesucht.de
was very helpfull, so very satisfied with that. The university (home or host) didn't offer any housing or recommended anything - so you were on your own. Think it was different for students having classes at Uni and not internships like me.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Lots of email during the time before my exchange - but everything was pretty clear. Maybe a little confusing what was for my home university and what was for the host university, but other than that fine. I got set up with a coordinator at the hospital, where I had my internship and they were very nice at putting together a schedule according to my wishes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinators at my home university was really a big help in the process - when I was unsure about the next step or information from my host uni, they were really good at clearing and confirming whatever I was unsure about.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Didn't take classes, but internship at hospital. I got the three department that I asked for and also during the time period that I wanted - this was through email correspondence with the coordinator at the hospital.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the instructions given by email - and don't stress about it. It takes some times but all the necessary informations and steps will be reach before arrival. Use your coordinator at your home university - they were super nice and very professionel.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: NA

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In general I find the internships in Denmark more well planned with good introductions to the department and information about your learning goals and expectations, which was not the case here. Depended a lot on the department and staff but in general the responsibility for learning is on yourself. When that said, the staff was very nice and there were lots of things to see, participate in and learn - you just have to be very outreaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Internship at hospital

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try and visit a couple of different departments. It is nice to see something different, but also nice to stay a bit longer in one place so you get more comfortable with the people, tasks, etc.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Lived up to my expectations.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Didn't use any, but I know that there were really good sport offers through the uni with many sports to choose from and affordable prices. 
There was a very nice canteen (Mensa) at the Uni, which was a really good hangout spot for students - sometimes events, flee markets etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Many nice cafes and bars to meet after uni. There are quite a lot of outdoor ping pong tables around Heidelberg which we enjoyed a lot for playing and hanging out. There is also some outdoor pools, which were nice to go to on warm days and also a really nice boulder hall a little outside of town. Spend time exploring the different neighborhoods.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the mountains around Heidelberg, Philosophenweg, Thingstätte. Take small trips to smaller towns along the Neckar. Visit Klosterhof (a nice small brewery in the hills). Just enjoy the cafes and bars of the city and make sure to visit the different neighbourhoods of the town.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In general life it was very easy. At the hospital it was more of a challenge, since they do some things so different from Denmark - but that was also something I really enjoyed; to see and experience all the differences. It also took me some months to feel comfortable in the German language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live with local students. I met a lot of people through the few German friends I got in the beginning - just say yes to everything people invite you to. Heidelberg is such a small town full of students, that you will meet the same people again and again, which make it very comfortable and easy to get to know people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Mostly the language. It was also a bit difficult to navigate in the hospital - what I was allowed to do, what was expected of me etc.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed living in a smaller town that still had such a vibrant student life with filled cafes and bars. Also getting an insight in a different health system through the internships was interesting.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Really try and speak the language even if you don't feel comfortable at first. It is really rewarding learning a new language and something I really enjoyed. Wished I had tried a little harder from the beginning.
- Spend the weekends in the city and explore the place you are living instead of traveling too much around. Heidelberg is such a beautiful place to live and many things too do
- Take a language course. You will meet a lot of people right away and get into the language quickly.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting out of my familiar settings and meeting some wonderfull new people. It was also very fun to learn a new language and experience the different culture in the hospital. Also living in such beautiful surroundings.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The internship required quite a lot of energy - it was in a new language, I had to be very outreaching and was commuting 45 min every morning (to Mannheim University Clinic).

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
